rows.abstract: In recognition of the invaluable services of the barangay day care center workers who continue to display serious commitment and who are at the forefront in the education and protection of  children, the bill proposes to grant them compulsory enrollment in the National Health Insurance Program (PhilHealth) and their dependents to receive and avail of an adequate package of essential health services.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 61, 62, 63 ANd 65 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6975 PLACING FOR THE PURPOSE THE PROVINCIAL JAILS UNDER THE JURISDICTION OF THE BUREAU OF JAIL MANAGEMENT AND PENOLOGY (BJMP) APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to remove from the provincial governments the supervision and control over  provincial and sub-provincial jails and place them with the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) to avoid confusion as to which government agency should be held responsible for the improvement of these jails and the discipline of its jail personnel.

rows.author: D003

rows.title_full: AN ACT ENHANCING THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUVENILE JUSTICE, CREATING THE OFFICE OF JUVENILE JUSTICE AND DELINQUENCY PREVENTION UNDER THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to establish a comprehensive juvenile justice system based on the recommendations of the National Convention on the Rights of Children to reform youth offenders and for the government to adhere to the international standards concerning juvenile justice.

rows.author: D003
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2006-08-07, transmitted to on 2006-08-14 and received by the Senate on 2006-08-14
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO STRENGTHEN AND PROPAGATE FOSTER CARE FOR ABANDONED AND NEGLECTED CHILDREN AND OTHER CHILDREN WITH SPECIAL NEEDS, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Foster Care Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Foster Care Act of 2004\".The bill seeks to sytematize and enhance foster care in the country by providing incentives to qualified foster familites such as subsidy from the government, health insurance and tax exemptions. If this bill is enacted into law, it will also accord a legal framework under which every abused, neglected, surrendered, dependent and abandoned child can be provided with an alternative family.

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING YOUTH CENTERS IN ALL FIFTEEN (15) REGIONS OF THE COUNTRY, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Youth Center Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Youth Center Act of 2004\". The bill provides for a concrete program that will alleviate the plight of the youth by establishing an integrated youth center in every region in the country to be utilized as transient shelters, lodging facilities and skills training centers for those who are in need of immediate assistance and attention.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on YOUTH AND SPORTS DEVELOPMENT since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING A THREE(3)-DAY NON-CUMMULATIVE LEAVE WITH PAY ANNUALLY TO EMPLOYED PARENTS TO ATTEND TO THE SPECIAL NEEDS OF THEIR CHILDREN
rows.title_short: Parental Leave Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Parental Leave Act of 2004\". The bill institutionalizes the grant of an annual three-day parental leave of absence with pay to working parents or guardians to enable them to attend to special circumstances involving their children or ward in any school activity.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF MUNICIPAL LIBRARIES IN ALL MUNICIPALITY NATIONWIDE
rows.abstract: The purpose of the bill is to give as many children as possible the chance to develop their potentials by providing them access to informative reading materials through the establishment of municipal libraries nationwide.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING CENTERS FOR STREET CHILDREN IN EVERY REGION OF THE PHILIPPINES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Declares it a State policy to prevent the exploitation of infants and children through mendicancy and provide rehabilitative service for those already exploited or in immediate danger of exploitation, and promote the rehabilitation of minors by providing an integrated development package of preventive, interceptive and/or remedial services.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING PROSTITUTION, DEFINING THE PERSONS LIABLE THEREFOR, PROVIDING MEASURES AND SUPPORT SERVICES FOR ITS VICTIMS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: The Anti-Prostitution Act
rows.abstract: \"The Anti-Prostitution Act\".  The bill seeks to end the continuing sexual exploitation of women and children and all forms of gender-based violence; recognizing prostitution as a human rights violation which calls for a coordinated and sustained response from all agencies of the government.  It imposes stiff penalties for prostitution and provides social services and programs to help victims of prostitution.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2004-07-28

rows.title_short: Anti-Rabies Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Rabies Act of 2004\". The bill provides for a system for the control and prevention of the spread and eventual eradication of rabies.

rows.title_full: AN ACT RENAMING THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE (PNP) RANKS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIXTY-NINE HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-FIVE, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT ACT OF 1990'
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to clarify the common confusion brought about by the change in the classification of different ranks in the Philippine National Police as provided for under RA 6975 that has resulted to an alarming, if not ridiculous, improper identification of the officers.

rows.author: D011
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE MONTHLY BENEFITS OF BARANGAY OFFICIALS AND PROVIDING ALLOWANCES TO BARANGAY TANODS, BARANGAY HEALTH WORKERS AND BARANGAY SOCIAL WORKERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE, THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: The bill provides for an increase in the monthly allowance granted to the punong barangay from PhP1,000.00 to PhP3,000.00 and to the sangguniang barangay members, barangay treasurer, and barangay secretary from PhP600.00 to PhP1,800.00. It also grants a PhP 1,500 monthly allowance to the lupong tagapamayapa, barangay tanods, barangay health workers and barangay social workers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D011
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING RETIREMENT BENEFITS TO ALL ELECTIVE OR APPOINTIVE BARANGAY OFFICIALS WHO HAVE RENDERED A CONSECUTIVE PERIOD OF NINE (9)YEARS OR THREE (3) TERMS OF PUBLIC SERVICE IN THE BARANGAY, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The bill entitles all elective and appointive barangay officials, who have rendered a consecutive period of nine (9) years or three (3) terms of honorable service, to receive a monthly pension for life amounting to not less than 65% of the monthly average honoraria, allowances and other emoluments authorized by law or barangay, municipal or city ordinance.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D011
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 66 OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 881, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: This bill requires that any person holding an appointive office or position, from the Department Secretary down to the Director level or their equivalent, who intends to run for an elective office, to resign from his position two (2) years prior to the next preceding election.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D011
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING THAT ALL CONTRACTUAL AND CASUAL EMPLOYEES IN THE GOVERNMENT SERVICE BE PAID THEIR CORRESPONDING WAGES DURING SPECIAL PUBLIC HOLIDAYS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The bill entitles all contractual and casual government employees, who have rendered at least six (6) months of continuous service, to payment of their corresponding daily wages for special public holidays as may be proclaimed by the President of the Philippines.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D011
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING CIVIL SERVICE ELIGIBILITY UNDER CERTAIN CONDITIONS TO A GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEE WHOSE STATUS OF APPOINTMENT IS CASUAL OR CONTRACTUAL AND WHO HAS RENDERED A TOTAL OF TEN (10) YEARS OF EFFICIENT SERVICE
rows.abstract: The bill grants civil service eligibility to all government employees who are holding career service positions appointed under casual or contractual status and who have rendered at least ten (10) years of efficient service. Directs the Civil Service Commission to formulate performance evaluation standards in order to determine those qualified to avail of the privilege granted under this act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D011
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR SURVIVORSHIP BENEFITS TO SURVIVING SPOUSE OF RETIRED JUSTICE-PENSIONER WHO DIES WHILE RECEIVING HIS MONTHLY PENSION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED NINE HUNDRED TEN, AS AMENDED, ENTITLED 'AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR THE RETIREMENT OF JUSTICES OF THE SUPREME COURT AND OF THE COURT OF APPEALS, FOR THE ENFORCEMENT OF THE PROVISIONS HEREOF BY THE GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE SYSTEM, AND TO REPEAL COMMONWEALTH ACT NUMBERED FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SIX'
rows.abstract: The bill provides that THE SURVIVING SPOUSE OF A RETIRED JUSTICE, WHO DIED AFTER RECEIVING RETIREMENT PENSION, SHALL BE PAID A MONTHLY PENSION EQUIVALENT TO EIGHTY PERCENT (80%) OF THE AMOUNT RECEIVED BY RETIRED JUSTICE-PENSIONER UNTIL THE SURVIVING SPOUSE REMARRIES OR DIES AND THE SURVIVING SPOUSE OF A JUSTICE WHO DIED WITHOUT HAVING RECEIVED RETIREMENT PENSION SHALL, IF SURVIVING SPOUSE DOES NOT REMARRY, ALSO BE PAID THE SAME PENSION MONTHLY WHEN THE SURVIVING SPOUSE REACHES THE AGE OF SIXTY-FIVE (65) AND UNTIL THE SURVIVING SPOUSE REMARRIES OR DIES, UNLESS THE SURVIVING SPOUSE IS ACTUALLY RECEIVING A SIMILAR PENSION FOR THE SAME CONSIDERATION FROM OTHER GOVERNMENT FUNDS.
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2006-02-22

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO MAXIMIZE THE COLLECTION OF REVENUES BY REQUIRING THE FILING OF STATEMENT OF ASSETS, LIABILITIES AND NETWORTH AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2003 AND BY GRANTING TAX AMNESTY ON ALL UNPAID INTERNAL REVENUE TAXES IMPOSED BY THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT FOR TAXABLE YEAR 2003 AND PRIOR YEARS
rows.abstract: This bill proposes a tax amnesty program which  aims to bring in a large number of corporate and individual taxpayers into the folds of national taxation. rows.title_short: Omnibus Housing and Urban Development Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Omnibus Housing and Urban Development Act of 2004\". The bill seeks to rationalize the housing program of the country to be able to reach out the broadest number of people, especially the  needy and marginalized ones. Creates the Department of Housing and Urban Development which is tasked to formulate and implement a comprehensive national urban development strategy and a national shelter strategy and to coordinate in delivering urban infrastructure, services and housing.

rows.title_short: Organic Farming Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Organic Farming Act of 2004\". The bill aims to institutionalize the gradual use of organic farm fertilizers and pesticides and eventually ease out the use of petrochemical farm inputs which render agricultural lands acidic and less productive. It encourages the farmers to revert to organic farming system in order to cut on agricultural costs as well as to save the degenerating natural environment in the countryside.

rows.title_short: Mother-Child Friendly Facility Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Mother-Child Friendly Facility Act of 2004\". Mandates every private company employing at least one hundred (100) women to establish a drop-in facility for non-school age children in the workplace to ensure their proper care while the mothers are disposing of their professional duties in the company.

rows.abstract: The bill aims to legitimize the status of children born to unmarried couples below eighteen (18) years old who remain illegitimate even after their parents eventually enter into a contract of marriage, by amending certain provisions in the Family Code of the Philippines in order for said parents to avoid tedious, expensive and time consuming way of legitimizing these children.

rows.abstract: \"Local Histories Research and Curriculum Integration Act of 2004\". rows.title_short: New Civil Registration Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"New Civil Registration Act of 2004\".  Documents concerning the civil status of persons such as birth certificate, death, marriage, and court decrees and orders have become essential instruments of every citizen. However, the basic law that governs this sytem is already outdated.  The bill aims to create a new system of civil registration to make it more responsive.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED 5173, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS AN ACT CREATING A PHILIPPINE COAST GUARD, PRESCRIBING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATING THE NECESSARY FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES BY ESTABLISHING A SEPARATE AND DISTINCT PHILIPPINE COAST GUARD SERVICE ATTACHED TO THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Philippine Coast Guard Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Philippine Coast Guard Act of 2004\". The bill intends to transfer the Philippine Coast Guard from the Philippine Navy to the Department of Transportation and Communications  to enable it  to concentrate on its functions of marine safety administration, marine environmental protection, marine search and rescue and maritime law enforcement. It is expected that said transfer would  result in a unified and integrated approach to maritime safety and water transport development.

rows.author: A040
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL CELLULAR AND WIRELESS TELEPHONE PROGRAM
rows.title_short: National Cellular and Wireless Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"National Cellular and Wireless Act of 2004\". The bill directs the Department of Transportation and Communications (DOTC) to implement a five-year (5 year) National Cellular and Wireless Telephone Program using a combination of government and private investments in an environment of free competition and mandatory interconnection. It further mandates that all landline telephone programs of the government be accordingly revised  and contracts under negotiation be programmed and redirected towards the enforcement of the program.

rows.title_short: Halal Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Halal Act of 2004\". The bill defines the term \"Halal\" as \"lawful,\" as pertaining to food or products permitted for human consumption under the Shariah Law. It establishes the general guidelines on the preparation, handling and verification of Halal products such as food, beverage, cosmetics, garments and textile which serve as a basic requirement for certification. It also includes the accreditation of abattoirs and outlets and other service establishments.

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING FROM TAXATION ALL DONATIONS, GRANTS OR GIFTS TO NON-STOCK AND NON-PROFIT EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS
rows.abstract: It grants FULL TAX EXEMPTION and TAX CREDITS to non-stock and non-profit educational institutions that actively support the educational institutions and programs of the government.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE PRACTICE OF PLUMBING ENGINEERING IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.title_short: Philippine Plumbing Engineering Act
rows.abstract: \"Philippine Plumbing Engineering Act.\" The bill updates the Plumbing Law of 1955 which regulates the trade of master plumber and confers licenses to high school graduates with five (5) years plumbing experience. With the advent of high-rise buildings, the demand has risen for master plumbers with engineering expertise. The bill seeks to elevate the plumbing trade to the level of professional engineering and to regulate the practice of the same.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C043
rows.mother_status: Senate agreed on Conference Committee Report on 2007-06-05
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE UNIVERSITY OF THE PHILIPPINES AS THE NATIONAL UNIVERSITY
rows.title_short: The University of the Philippines Charter
rows.abstract: \"The University of the Philippines Charter\". The measure strengthens the University of the Philippines by declaring it a policy of the State to promote, foster, nurture and protect the right of all citizens to quality education.

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING AUTOMATIC PROMOTION OF GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES UPON RETIREMENT FROM GOVERNMENT SERVICE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill aims to give due recognition to government officials and employees who have been in the government service for more than twenty (20) years despite their meager salaries, by promoting them one grade higher at the time of their retirement. The adjusted salary grade level shall be used as the basis in computing his retirement pay.

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING INFLUENCE PEDDLING AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Anti-Influence Peddling Act
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Influence Peddling Act.\" The bill defines influence peddling as an act of representing oneself, either orally or in writing, as being able, whether real or imagined, to influence, facilitate or assist another person having some business, transaction, application, request or contract with the government in which a public official or employee has to intervene. It seeks to penalize any person who engages in influence peddling.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING EARLY CHILDHOOD DEVELOPMENT AND EDUCATION CENTERS FOR CHILDREN AGED ZERO (0)TO FIVE (5)YEARS, CREATING THE IMPLEMENTING MACHINERY THEREOF, PROVIDING GUIDELINES, INCENTIVES, GOVERNMENT FINANCIAL SUPPORT AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Early Childhood Development and Education Act
rows.abstract: \"Early Childhood Development and Education Act.\" The bill seeks to establish Early Childhood Development Centers which will develop a program of activities that will focus primarily on the total development of children with their first language as their medium of instruction; provide the parents with training programs which focuses endeavor to inculcate responsble parenthood and provide guidance in child rearing, health, nutrition and education.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 2004-07-28
